title: Built a 33-minigame Whac-A-Mole with GenAI and open-source tools — here is what I learned the hard way
author: Mecanos3
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I just finished making a modernized Whac-A-Mole game that includes 33 mini-games, and I wanted to share my experience using AI for it.

I generated base images and GIFs with prompts, but honestly, getting consistent sprite sheets was a nightmare. I had to spend a ton of time editing and tweaking everything in Photopea and other open-source tools to make it look cohesive.

On the coding side, AI helped me learn a lot of dev techniques while building all these mini-games. But writing perfect code with AI is way harder than people think. My main script eventually hit around 5,000 lines, and at that point, you can't just ask an AI to fix or rewrite stuff anymore. I had to actually dig in, understand the code, and debug it myself.

It was a huge learning curve, but it really made me want to move on to my dream project next: a full 3D game.

If anyone wants to try it out and drop some feedback, I'd really appreciate it! Also curious to know how you guys manage consistency and large codebases when working with AI?
